text_blocks.snippet: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems and machines. As defined by the Stanford Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI) Program, it encompasses any computer system capable of performing tasks that normally require human cognition, such as learning, reasoning, pattern recognition, and decision-making.
snippet_highlighted_words: the simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems and machines

list.snippet: Machine Learning (ML): Algorithms that find patterns in data and improve their performance over time without being explicitly programmed.
Deep Learning: A subset of machine learning using multilayered neural networks modeled after the human brain to process complex data like images, voice, and text.
Generative AI: Advanced models—such as Large Language Models (LLMs)—that generate new content, code, or media based on prompts.
Artificial Narrow Intelligence (ANI): Systems designed to handle a specific, single task (like web search, GPS navigation, or virtual assistants). Most modern AI belongs to this category.
Artificial General Intelligence (AGI): A theoretical system that matches human cognitive flexibility across any intellectual task.
Artificial Superintelligence (ASI): A hypothetical future state where AI surpasses human intelligence across all domains.
Everyday Tools: Search engines, smartphone personal assistants (like Siri), and predictive text.
Industry & Science: Medical diagnostics, genomic research, financial modeling, and autonomous transportation.
Content & Language: Real-time translation, image generation, and automated text summaries.

perspectives.author: evolving.ai
perspectives.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicts that cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease, and mental illness could become diseases of the past within the next decade, thanks to artificial intelligence. Speaking in Anthropic's IPO roadshow video, Amodei said AI could help humanity solve medical problems that have remained out of reach for thousands of years. He believes AI could speed up medical research so much that 50 to 100 years of scientific progress could happen in just 5 to 10 years. This includes discovering new treatments, understanding diseases at a deeper level, and developing drugs far faster than traditional methods allow. Anthropic is already expanding its work in medicine and biology, using Claude to help researchers study complex biological systems and identify promising new treatments.
